comment: Site plan shows overhead electric conductors (OHE) running along western and southern boundaries near proposed buildings, but no clearance dimensions from the outer conductor to any building face are provided. No horizontal sky-to-ground clearance dimensions are documented on plan or elevation sheets. Add dimension annotations on site plan and building elevation sheets showing minimum 7.5-foot horizontal clearance from outside conductor to all building edges.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 and adjacent overhead electric conductors on western and southern site boundaries

comment: Overhead electric lines (OHE) are shown on plans but are not labeled with voltage classification. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies only to distribution facilities operating below 60kV (typically 12.47kV or 34.5kV in Austin). Without voltage labeling, the applicability of this distribution-specific requirement cannot be determined. Verify whether shown OHE lines are distribution or transmission facilities and label with operating voltage on utility plans.
applicableAreas: Buildings and facilities proximate to overhead electric lines

comment: No building elevation views are provided showing the vertical relationship between building projections and overhead electric conductors. Site plan (Sheet 9) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) show OHE lines and building footprints but lack elevation views documenting clearances. Both 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from building projections to outside conductor must be verified. Provide building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor elevations and dimension callouts showing clearances from all building projections.
applicableAreas: Building roofs, overhangs, awnings, balconies, and canopies on Buildings 1-8 proximate to overhead electric conductors

comment: Buildings are proposed near Valley View Road where existing overhead electric facilities are shown. Plans contain general Austin Energy boilerplate notes acknowledging responsibility for maintaining clearances but do not document that specific 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances from OHE to buildings in the ROW-adjacent area have been verified and met. Provide dimension callouts on site plan and building elevations demonstrating compliance with both clearance envelopes from OHE to each building edge within potential clearance distance of ROW facilities.
applicableAreas: Buildings near Valley View Road right-of-way where overhead electric facilities are located or will be relocated

comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the site plan package showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations and locations. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility pole locations but provides no conductor elevation data. Building elevation sheets with registered surveyor data showing conductor heights and clearance dimensions to building faces and projections are required to verify vertical clearance compliance. Provide building elevations with surveyed conductor elevation callouts.
applicableAreas: All buildings within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities

comment: Section and profile views with dimension callouts from the outside conductor to building edges are absent from the site plan. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 is a water/wastewater utility tap plan, not electrical clearance profiles. No dimension lines originating at conductor locations and extending to outermost building edges are provided on any sheet. Provide section/profile exhibits with specific clearance dimensions from outside conductor to all building faces and projections.
applicableAreas: All buildings, structures, and building projections within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities

comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows fencing (identified by H.6 key notes for wooden privacy fences) but provides no clearance dimension callouts from the fence faces to outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No dimension annotations demonstrate the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance. Provide dimension callouts on site plan and fence detail sheets showing clearance from outside conductor to fence face and posts.
applicableAreas: Privacy fences and site perimeter fencing shown on landscape plan near overhead electric conductors

comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility pole locations. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows fence alignments. However, no dimension callouts document the horizontal distance from fence posts to existing electric poles. Plans must show that fence posts are located minimum 10 feet from pole centerlines. Provide dimension annotations on site/landscape plan showing distance from each fence post location to nearest utility pole.
applicableAreas: Fence post locations on site where existing utility poles are present

comment: Transmission notes on Sheet 3, Block 9 indicate transmission facilities exist on or adjacent to site, but no clear transmission line routing map is provided showing easement boundaries relative to proposed fencing. Without voltage confirmation and transmission easement delineation, cannot determine whether fences are beneath/within transmission easement and therefore subject to non-conductive material and grounding requirements. Verify transmission line locations, provide transmission easement boundary on site plan, confirm fence specifications (non-conductive material and grounding details) if within easement.
applicableAreas: Fencing shown in proximity to electric transmission lines if transmission easement applies

comment: Site plan (Sheet 9) and wall plan sheets show retaining walls at multiple locations on the site near OHE lines, but no clearance dimension callouts demonstrate the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outermost conductor to wall face. Provide dimension annotations on site plan and wall section sheets showing clearance from outside conductor to outermost edge of retaining wall.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls shown on site plan near overhead electric conductors

comment: Wall plan (Sheets 38 and 39) shows retaining wall section views and details but these cross-sections do not include dimension callouts from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines to the outermost edge of retaining wall faces. Section views showing clearance dimensions from conductor to wall are required for compliance verification. Provide section views of all retaining walls with clearance dimension annotations from outside conductor location.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities

comment: Grading plan (Sheet 11) and site plan (Sheet 9) show driveway alignments and elevations, but no cross-section views document vertical clearance from finished driveway surface to lowest point of overhead electric conductors (including telecommunications attachments). The 16-foot minimum clearance (parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot clearance (areas with truck traffic) must be verified through section views with dimension callouts. Provide section views showing driveway finished grade elevation and overhead line clearance dimensions; verify whether truck traffic is expected.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveways near overhead electric lines where vertical clearance applies

comment: Site plan shows parking areas and driveways, and grading plan shows finished surface elevations, but no section views document vertical clearance from parking pad surface to overhead electric lines. Plans must include section views with dimension callouts showing clearance from parking pad elevation to lowest overhead conductor point (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, 18 feet with truck traffic, 12 feet minimum for residential pedestrian areas). Additionally, a note on plans must identify the clearance requirement. Provide section views with vertical clearance dimensions and a plan note documenting required clearance.
applicableAreas: Vehicle parking and display areas on concrete pads beneath overhead electric lines

comment: Sheet 3, Block 9 indicates transmission facilities are present and notes restrictions for areas within 25 feet of transmission structures. Grading plan shows driveway and road surface elevations but provides no section views documenting 30-foot minimum vertical clearance from road/driveway surface to electric transmission lines. Verify transmission line locations, provide transmission easement boundary on plans, and provide section views showing road/driveway elevation with vertical clearance dimension to transmission lines (minimum 30 feet).
applicableAreas: Roads and driveways beneath transmission lines

comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles along the western property boundary near Valley View Road. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows driveway alignments, but no notes or dimensions address whether existing poles are in conflict with driveways or require relocation. If existing poles are within or immediately adjacent to proposed driveway alignments, poles must be relocated minimum 30 feet from driveway edge. Provide dimension callouts showing pole locations relative to driveway edges, or provide relocation notes if poles will be moved.
applicableAreas: Existing electric poles that conflict with or are immediately adjacent to proposed driveway alignments

comment: Critical requirement: all clearance dimensions must be measured from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR, never from utility pole centerline. Multi-conductor installations have conductors offset several feet from pole center. Currently, no clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheets, so this measurement methodology cannot be verified. When clearance dimensions are provided, ensure dimension lines originate at the conductor location (not pole center) and extend to the outermost edge of the site feature being cleared.
applicableAreas: Any clearance dimensions shown on site plan sheets

comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles along Valley View Road frontage. Site plan shows sidewalk alignments along the property boundary. However, no dimension callouts or notes verify that sidewalks are cleared from existing power poles at each end of the property along right-of-way. Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing distance from sidewalk edges to pole locations at north and south property limits, or provide relocation/adjustment notes if poles are in conflict.
applicableAreas: Sidewalks at property ends along right-of-way frontage near existing power poles

comment: For a 39-unit multi-family project, trash receptacles or enclosures are expected but their specific locations are not clearly documented on site plan in relationship to overhead electric lines. If trash bins are located beneath overhead conductors, raised trash bins during service collection must maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from the outer conductor. Identify trash collection locations on site plan with dimension callouts showing clearance from OHE, or provide notes confirming trash areas are outside the clearance zone.
applicableAreas: Trash enclosure and receptacle locations on site

comment: UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition: customer facilities shall NOT be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, distinct from the clearance distance requirements and independent of measured clearance. Existing survey shows OHE lines; site plan shows buildings and structures in proximity. Plans must affirmatively demonstrate that no buildings, building projections, overhangs, or other permanent structures are positioned directly beneath or above the overhead distribution conductor routing. Any facility within electric easement must maintain 7.5-foot clearance. Provide clearance verification on all plan sheets showing OHE routing relative to structures.
applicableAreas: All buildings, structures, and site features relative to overhead distribution electric lines shown on site boundary

comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical meter locations but does not document water meter locations relative to overhead electric service-drop conductors. Water meters must maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor of service drops. Provide utility plan with water meter locations dimensioned from overhead service-drop routing, or confirm water meters are located clear of service drop conductor zone.
applicableAreas: Water meter locations relative to overhead electric service drops

comment: Site plan shows building footprints and property lines. Existing and proposed electric facilities require clearance space in areas adjacent to property. Permanent foundations within 5 feet of property line may not allow necessary clearance space for electric utility facilities and their future maintenance access. Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing distance from building foundation edges to property line, particularly where electric poles or facilities are located adjacent to property boundary, or confirm that adequate clearance space is maintained for utility access.
applicableAreas: Permanent building foundations located within 5 feet of property line

comment: Vertical clearances from overhead electric lines to buildings, driveways, and parking areas appear potentially marginal based on site elevations and estimated overhead line heights shown on existing survey. No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data is provided. When overhead lines cross or are adjacent to site features with height constraints (driveways requiring 16-18 feet, buildings requiring clearance), a registered professional surveyor must provide measured pole and conductor elevation data showing actual mid-span clearances. Hire registered surveyor to conduct mid-span clearance survey showing actual conductor elevations and clearances to all site features.
applicableAreas: All locations where overhead electric lines are adjacent to proposed buildings, driveways, parking, or other structures with vertical clearance concerns

comment: Landscape plan shows outdoor lighting fixtures but does not document clearances from these fixtures to overhead electric conductors. Both 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance must be verified. Site plan notes state decorative lighting must be full cut-off and fully shielded per Land Development Code, but clearance from overhead lines is not addressed. Provide dimension callouts on landscape plan showing clearance from light fixture locations to outside conductor, or provide relocation notes for fixtures within clearance zones.
applicableAreas: Decorative outdoor lighting fixture locations near overhead electric lines

comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows trees in proximity to overhead electric line (OHE) running along southern and eastern boundaries, identified only by classification codes (M, SY, PL) without species identification. No lateral distances from trees to conductors are documented. Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors (or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors) must be from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, species marked 'UC', generally mature height ≤20 feet). Provide tree species identification on landscape plan by reference to plant schedule (Sheet 32 or detailed plant list), verify species against ECM Appendix F utility-compatible list, and document lateral distances from trees to OHE. Relocate any non-compatible trees outside the clearance zones.
applicableAreas: Tree planting locations on landscape plan near overhead electric distribution and transmission conductors

comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles with guy wire symbols (support cables from poles to ground anchors), indicating down guy presence. However, site plan does not address whether down guys are in conflict with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or other site features, or whether they have been relocated or poles converted to self-supporting structures. Down guy wires and anchor locations must be verified against all proposed site features and either relocated or resolved through pole conversion. Provide down guy relocation notes or conversion specifications for any poles with down guys that conflict with site improvements.
applicableAreas: Down guy wire anchor locations shown on existing survey conflicting with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or other site features

comment: Sheet 3, Block 9 (Electric Transmission Notes) indicates transmission structures are present on or adjacent to site. Transmission structures often require angled down guy wires extending to ground anchors. Easement exhibit must show dedicated easement for transmission down guy anchors extending 10 feet either side of guy wire alignment plus minimum 50 feet beyond end of anchor point. Verify transmission structure down guy anchor locations and provide transmission guy anchor easement dimensions on plat/easement exhibit.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor locations for transmission structure support cables

comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles with guy wire symbols indicating down guy anchors. Site plan and easement exhibit must show dedicated down guy anchor easements (10-foot wide extending minimum 5 feet past ground entry point of anchor) for each down guy anchor visible on survey. If down guys are relocated or removed, provide relocation notes. Provide down guy anchor easement exhibits showing 10-foot width and minimum 5-foot extension from each visible down guy anchor on existing survey.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from distribution poles on site

comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer locations on the site but does not provide section views showing vertical clearance from top of transformer equipment to overhead electric lines. Transformers must maintain minimum 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor of overhead lines. Provide section views of transformer locations showing vertical clearance dimension from top of transformer to lowest point of overhead conductor.
applicableAreas: Transformer equipment (pad-mounted or pole-mounted) shown on electrical design plan in relation to overhead electric lines

comment: During construction, staging areas, crane swing radii, material storage, scaffold locations, and equipment operation zones must maintain 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333. This is a working clearance requirement distinct from permanent clearances. No construction phasing plan or logistics plan has been provided in the site plan package showing staging area boundaries and confirming 10-foot working clearance during all construction phases. Provide construction logistics plan or phasing plan showing staging areas and confirming 10-foot radial clearance from OHE during all construction phases.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platforms during site construction

comment: Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 requires plans to include a note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines. This note is not present on the cover sheet or general notes sheets. Review of Sheets 1 and 3 found no such notification requirement. Add a general note on cover sheet stating: 'Owner/Contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before commencement of any work near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.'
applicableAreas: Cover sheet or general notes for project with overhead electric lines and construction activities

comment: For residential service-mast through-roof installations with voltages ≤300V, clearance requirements differ: 3-foot minimum above roof, or 18-inch minimum if mast is within 4 feet of roof edge. No building elevation sheets showing service-mast through-roof installations have been provided in the site plan package. If service masts are proposed through roofs, building elevation sheets must document mast locations and roof clearance dimensions. If service masts are not used (all underground service), this requirement is not applicable. Clarify service installation method and provide elevation documentation if roof-mounted masts are proposed.
applicableAreas: Service-mast through-roof installations on proposed buildings

comment: Landscape plan shows mitigation trees (marked 'M') near the overhead electric distribution line (OHE) on south edge, but plant schedule does not indicate which specific tree species are located at each 'M' position. Utility-compatible status of proposed trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) cannot be verified without cross-referencing species against ECM Appendix F utility-compatible designations and confirming specific species placement locations on landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Area south of site along overhead electric distribution conductor

comment: Utility pole locations are not depicted on the landscape plan. The plan's key notes do not include a pole symbol, and no poles are explicitly labeled or shown. Without pole locations on the landscape plan, proximity of trees to poles cannot be verified. This is particularly critical because poles may be located off-site (on adjacent public right-of-way) but still require the 10-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: Locations where overhead electric poles may be present

comment: Electrical transformer pads are shown with specific locations on Sheet 21 (electrical plan), but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not overlay or cross-reference these equipment locations. The landscape plan shows proposed trees but does not indicate which trees are within 10 feet of the transformer pads shown on Sheet 21. The two plans must be analyzed together to verify clearances, but no cross-referencing or overlay is provided.
applicableAreas: Locations of electrical transformer pads and pad-mounted equipment

comment: Electrical pull boxes and underground routing are shown on Sheet 21 (electrical plan), but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not overlay or cross-reference these locations. The 5-lateral-foot clearance from underground equipment cannot be verified without explicit cross-referencing of underground equipment locations to proposed tree locations on the landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Locations of underground electric equipment and pull boxes

comment: Root barrier requirement applies only to trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. The specific locations of underground equipment relative to proposed trees are not cross-referenced between the electrical plan (Sheet 21) and landscape plan (Sheet 31). Therefore, which trees (if any) require root barriers cannot be determined. Additionally, landscape detail sheets (Sheet 37) do not specify root barrier requirements for any plantings.
applicableAreas: Locations of underground electric equipment within 20 feet of proposed trees

comment: The landscape plan designates trees near the overhead electric line with a generic 'M' (mitigation tree) symbol. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 provides overall tree species and quantities but does not cross-reference which specific species are placed at each 'M' location on the landscape plan. Trees proposed near overhead electric facilities must be identified by species on or near the landscape plan to allow verification of utility-compatibility and clearance compliance. The current documentation requires cross-referencing two separate sheets to determine species identification, which does not constitute adequate plan notation per standard reviewer practice.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan Sheet 31 and plant schedule Sheet 35

comment: No clearance distance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan between proposed trees and the overhead electric distribution conductor (OHE). Per UCM § 1.10.10.4, clearances must be measured from the tree trunk center to the outside conductor (not pole centerline). The landscape plan must include dimension lines and annotations specifying the lateral clearance distances to confirm compliance with distribution clearance zones (< 15 feet restricted, 15-25 feet restricted for non-UC or large trees, > 25 feet unrestricted). Provide dimensions from tree trunk symbols to the overhead electric conductor line.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan Sheet 31, area along south property edge with overhead electric line

comment: While the landscape plan does show tree symbols (as circles with center points), no dimension lines or clarifying notes indicate whether any clearance measurements shown or made are measured from the tree trunk (planting location, center of circle) or from the projected canopy edge. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires measurement from trunk center, not canopy edge. To prevent ambiguity, landscape plan callouts and dimension lines must explicitly clarify the measurement origin point.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan Sheet 31, area along south property edge

comment: No documented written approval from Austin Energy is provided in the submitted plans authorizing any trees to be planted within the restricted clearance zones established by UCM § 1.10.10.4. This item is conditionally applicable: if trees are determined to violate clearance restrictions (per evaluations of EL-2.1, EL-2.3, EL-2.6, EL-2.7, EL-2.8), then explicit Austin Energy approval would be required. Since the tree species and exact placement cannot be verified (per EL-2.1 and EL-2.10 findings), and clearances are not dimensioned (per EL-2.12/EL-2.13), it cannot be determined whether trees are actually within prohibited zones. Therefore, applicability of this approval requirement cannot be established.
applicableAreas: Trees proposed near overhead electric distribution conductor and equipment

comment: Specific horizontal clearance dimensions from transformer pads to buildings, structures, and building foundations are not shown or dimensioned on the electrical design plan. While five transformer pads are clearly labeled and located, no measurements indicating compliance with minimum 5-foot clearance requirements are provided.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

comment: Site plan shows retaining walls on the grading plan (Sheet 11). Specific horizontal clearance dimensions from transformer pads to retaining walls are not dimensioned on the electrical or grading plans.
applicableAreas: Retaining wall locations on site

comment: Site plan shows various features but no fences or gates are clearly identified as directly adjacent to transformer pad locations. Fence locations and transformer access door orientations are not sufficiently documented to evaluate clearances.
applicableAreas: Areas adjacent to transformer pads with fences

comment: Plans do not clearly show whether clearances less than 5 feet to buildings are proposed. No architectural specifications or fire rating documentation is provided to support any reduced clearance approvals.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad clearance areas

comment: Building elevations showing balconies and overhangs relative to transformer pad locations were not reviewed. Vertical clearance documentation above transformer pads is not provided.
applicableAreas: Buildings with balconies or overhangs above transformer locations

comment: Building elevations and windows/door locations relative to transformer pads were not examined. This requirement applies to oil-filled equipment but transformer type specifications are not provided on the electrical plan.
applicableAreas: Building facades with windows, doors, or ventilating ducts

comment: Site plan indicates sidewalks throughout the development, but specific dimensions from transformer pad edges to sidewalk back-of-curb are not shown or dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Sidewalk locations adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Building floor plans and stairwell locations were not examined. This is a residential townhome project; exterior stairwells serving as fire exits are not typical for this building type.
applicableAreas: Building stairwells near transformer locations

comment: Building elevations showing fire escape or external stairwell locations were not reviewed. Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on the electrical plan.
applicableAreas: Fire escapes and external stairwells

comment: Transformer pad locations are shown on the electrical plan, but specific clearance dimensions from the access door side to adjacent buildings or open areas are not provided. Access door orientation is not indicated on the plan.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad access door sides

comment: No transformer locations are proposed in niches, vaults, or enclosed areas (building footprints). All visible transformer pads appear to be surface-mounted in open site areas.
applicableAreas: Transformer locations in confined spaces or niches

comment: Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) was not detailed in review. Fire hydrant locations relative to transformer pad locations cannot be evaluated without reviewing that sheet.
applicableAreas: Fire hydrant locations near transformer pads

comment: Landscape plan shows overhead electric line (OHE) with trees nearby, and proposed plant species are listed on Sheet 35. However, complete species identification is not confirmed for all trees within 15-foot radius of overhead distribution lines or within 10 feet of transformer pads. Tree species utility-compatibility verification against ECM Appendix F is incomplete.
applicableAreas: Trees within 10 feet of transformer pads and 15 feet of overhead electric lines

comment: Landscape plan shows general planting areas but specific clearance distances from shrubs and vegetation to transformer pad access doors are not dimensioned. Planting schedule lists shrub species and maximum spacing but does not specify proximity to specific transformer pad access doors.
applicableAreas: Landscape areas adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Landscape plan shows tree locations and proposed species. Root barrier details and specifications are not shown on the landscape detail sheets reviewed.
applicableAreas: Trees within 20 feet of underground electric equipment

comment: Site plan shows general lighting requirements and fixtures. Photometric plan was not reviewed. Specific light pole locations relative to transformer pads are not shown or dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Light pole locations near transformers

comment: Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) was not detailed. Fire lane designations and their proximity to transformer pads cannot be evaluated.
applicableAreas: Fire lane designations

comment: Five transformer pads are shown on the electrical plan. Specific clearance dimensions between adjacent transformer pads are not shown or dimensioned on the plans.
applicableAreas: Multiple transformer pad locations

comment: Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) shows water line routing but specific clearance dimensions between transformer pads and water lines are not shown or dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Water utility line locations relative to transformer pads

comment: Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) shows wastewater line routing but specific clearance dimensions between transformer pads and wastewater lines are not shown or dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Wastewater utility line locations relative to transformer pads

comment: Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12) shows storm drain line routing but specific clearance dimensions between transformer pads and storm drain lines are not shown or dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Storm drain utility line locations relative to transformer pads

comment: Gas service infrastructure and pressure specifications are not clearly shown on the electrical or utility plans reviewed. Specific gas line locations relative to transformer pads cannot be evaluated.
applicableAreas: Gas line locations near transformer pads

comment: Utility plans show general routing of water, wastewater, and electric lines but do not provide specific dimension documentation of 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearances between transformer pads and other underground utilities (phone, cable, data, etc.).
applicableAreas: Underground utility locations near transformer pads

comment: Plans do not show architectural details or cross-sections depicting foundations, slabs, or underground structures relative to utility lines and transformer locations. Conflict verification documentation is not provided.
applicableAreas: Underground facilities and building foundations

comment: Landscape plan shows overhead electric line (OHE) symbol on the site. Specific horizontal sky-to-ground clearance dimensions (minimum 7.5 feet) from transformer pads to overhead distribution primary, neutral, and secondary conductors are not documented.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution line locations

comment: Overhead electric line (OHE) is shown on landscape plan but specific 15-foot radius clearance measurements from transformer locations to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors (measured from conductors, not pole centerline) are not dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution conductor locations

comment: Cross-section drawings are not provided showing vertical clearances in access paths above transformer locations. This is a required survey document for AE Design verification.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (survey requirement as required by AE Design)
applicableAreas: Access paths with overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas

comment: Grading plan (Sheet 11) shows general drainage slopes but does not specify whether transformer equipment is oil-filled or dry-type. Transformer specifications are not provided on the electrical plan. Drainage direction relative to building structures from oil-filled equipment cannot be verified without transformer type identification.
applicableAreas: Oil-filled transformer pad locations

comment: Vision analysis confirms that at least one transformer pad (located east of Unit 404/504, between Buildings 4 and 5) intersects or is located within a "25' Drainage Easement" (Doc. 2011021707) and an "Existing 15' Wastewater Easement" (Vol. 73, Pg. 76). Transformer pads cannot be located in drainage easements, water easements, sewer easements, or electrical easements under overhead lines without written Austin Energy Design approval. No such approval is documented on the plans.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad located east of Buildings 4-5, intersecting drainage/wastewater easements

comment: Only one transformer easement is explicitly labeled on the plan: a "Vault Easement" near Building 8. Other transformer pad locations do not show clearly labeled easements. No easement widths are dimensioned or specified, and Austin Energy accessibility requirements are not documented.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (additional clearance and access easements may be required)
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

comment: Vision analysis confirms that the electrical line routing from the transformer pad west of Building 2 to the electrical meters on Building 1 crosses through an area labeled "Wastewater Easement" on the electrical plan. Electrical routing must be 100% on private property. Routing through an easement violates this requirement unless easement routing is approved by the utility holding the easement.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer west of Building 2 to meters on Building 1

comment: Specific transformer pad dimensions are not shown or labeled on the electrical design plan. Service type specification (single-phase vs. three-phase) is not provided on the electrical plan. Without these specifications and without reference to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets, compliance with AE Design pad dimension requirements cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

comment: Vision analysis confirms that at least two transformer pads are located immediately adjacent to (within 4 feet of) parking areas and drive aisles: (1) west of Building 1, near the curved drive entrance, and (2) between Buildings 6 and 7, adjacent to the internal east-west drive aisle. Per the plans reviewed, no bollards are shown to protect these transformer pads. 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts are required where pads are within 4 feet of parking/vehicle circulation routes per AE Design equipment pad details.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads west of Building 1 and between Buildings 6-7, located near parking and drive aisles

comment: Overhead distribution line locations are shown on the landscape plan (OHE symbol). No customer facilities (buildings, parking garages, light poles, signs, structures) are clearly identified as being positioned directly under or over overhead distribution lines based on the site plan layout.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution line areas
